paragraphs: The G63 AMG has been the high-performance flagship of the G-Class range since 2012. The 2012–2018 W463-generation model uses the M157 — a 5.5-litre twin-turbo V8 that was the pinnacle of Mercedes-AMG's V8 engineering of that era. It's a different engine from both the naturally-aspirated M156 that preceded it in other AMG models and the newer M177 4.0-litre unit that replaced it from 2018. The M157 is known for valve seal and coolant system wear at higher mileages — which is why we replace those components as standard on every rebuild, alongside the timing chains and bearings.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every G63 AMG on the road.

cards.body: A 5.5-litre twin-turbo V8 fitted to the G63 AMG across the 2012–2018 W463 generation — the same M157 family confirmed elsewhere in the AMG V8 range (S-Class, CLS, E-Class). Known for valve seal and coolant system wear over time. We replace valve seals, timing chains, coolant components and bearings as standard on every M157 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: The G63 AMG's M157 engine is specific to the 2012–2018 W463 generation. Fitting a later M177 4.0-litre unit — or assuming parts from the M156 or M177 will work — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:
